newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller says opposition short of majority.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller says opposition short of majority.

text.p: Turkish conservative leader Tansu Ciller said on Thursday that her opponents in a fight to form a new coalition government did not have enough backing to win a confidence vote in parliament.
"They have not established a majority and it is not clear who would be their prime minister," Foreign Minister Ciller told a news conference.

Ciller is a main contender to be chosen by President Suleyman Demirel to forge a new coalition from the splintered parliament following Wednesday's resignation of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
She has the backing of Erbakan's Islamists for a plan to head a caretaker administration and take Turkey to early elections.
"The 55th government will be an election government. Parliament will take this decision," said Ciller, Erbakan's coalition partner for the last year.

A revamped alliance headed by Ciller would command the support on paper of 282 MPs in the 550-member assembly. Her main opponent, Motherland Party leader Mesut Yilmaz, only has 129 MPs and is not guaranteed of support from other secularist parties.
